findings.evidence: Table 7-1, row "3×H100 total VRAM", derivation cell reads in full: "3× the vendor's 80 GB per-part constant [1P][FACT] (NVIDIA H100 80 GB specification); tagged as the 2× and 8× rows and the 640 GB pool in Table 7-2 are" — the sentence ends on the word "are" with no predicate, and the same table's "2×H100 total VRAM" and "8×H100 total VRAM" rows carry complete derivations ("2 ×80 GB = 160 GB [1P][FACT] (NVIDIA H100 80 GB specification)", "8 ×80 GB = 640 GB [1P][FACT] (NVIDIA H100 80 GB specification)").
findings.issue: Truncated/incomplete derivation cell: the 3×H100 row's label text is missing its ending clause (apparently a note such as "…are tagged [1P][FACT] as well"), leaving a dangling predicate. Because this table is the book's anchor memory ledger, a half-finished label under a numeric row that feeds the "≥3×H100" conclusion is a visible production defect.
findings.fix_instruction: Complete the 3×H100 derivation cell (e.g. "3 × 80 GB = 240 GB [1P][FACT] (NVIDIA H100 80 GB specification); like the 2× and 8× rows and the 640 GB pool in Table 7-2, the capacity is a [1P][FACT] vendor constant") and proof the table for other truncated cells.

findings.issue: The text contains a formatting error in Section 7.7. There is a bullet point character '•' followed by an empty line or space, and then the next item '(a) decode-time...' is formatted as a separate line rather than a second bullet item, or the first bullet was left incomplete.
findings.fix_instruction: Correct the list formatting in Section 7.7 to ensure items are consistently bulleted.

findings.chapter: Ch. 7 — Memory Is the First Constraint
findings.evidence: PDF p.161 says: “The 24 GB device is an illustrative placeholder with no vendor model named, and no number from this subsection is used anywhere else in the book — it is a geometry example, not a hardware recommendation.” The same subsection later says: “Device capacities are first-party specifications (Intel Arc Pro B70 datasheet, B65 datasheet, Arc Pro B60 datasheet), retrieved 2026-10-28.”
findings.issue: The subsection first says no vendor model is named, then names vendor device datasheets in support of the same capacity discussion. This is a local provenance/clarity contradiction about whether the 24 GB device example is vendor-neutral or vendor-backed.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the first sentence so it says the device is illustrative rather than claiming no vendor model is named, or explicitly separate the unnamed 24 GB placeholder from the later named device-capacity examples.
